page.overview:
What is You Know My Name?

Abbey Road Studios|genre = Novelty|length = 4:21|label = Apple Records|writer = Lennon-McCartney|producer = George Martin}} You Know My Name (Look Up the Number) is a song by The Beatles. It was written by John Lennon and Paul McCartney and credited to Lennon/McCartney. It was originally released on the B-Side to the Let It Be single in March 1970. The song itself dates all the way back to 1967, where it would be recorded on a four-track with them all around a microphone. It is also only available in mono, as no stereo mix was ever made (the reason why is unknown). The song is on the "Past Masters" compilation, volume 2, (on the 2009 remaster, it is on disc 2) and on Anthology 2 as a sightly longer version. A 6-minute version of this song could be found on YouTube in 2012, but is unsurprisingly long gone, although uploads of the Past Masters version are still available.

The song is a music hall comedy number and is perhaps the silliest song in the Beatles' catalogue. Lennon came up with the lyrics and title after seeing a phone book.

McCartney once told Beatles recording analyst Mark Lewisohn, "[People] are only just discovering things like 'You Know My Name (Look Up the Number)' — probably my favourite Beatles' track!"

The song features a saxophone solo played by the Rolling Stones' Brian Jones.
